# FINAL ANALYSIS RECOMMENDED BY LAUREN DYKMAN

# Steps:

# 1) Test pairwise correlation of all abiotic factors. This will be used later.

# 2) Run global model with all main categorical experimental factors required (treatment, gravel size, month), all 2-way interactions between main categorical experimental factors, plus all abiotic and biotic factors.

# 3) Perform backwards elimination to choose model that minimizes AIC, sequentially removing factor with highest p-value and re-running model.

# 4) If final model includes two factors that co-vary, start again from step (2) but remove the least significant (highest p-value) of the co-varying factors from the global model.

# 5) Repeat until you reach a final model that minimizes the AIC that does not contain covarying factors.

# Define function for selecting significant fixed effects
```{r}
select.model <- function(df, response, required.predictors, predictors, random, stat.dist) {
  
  # df = your data frame
  # response = your response variable as a string, e.g. "kelp_length_cm"
  # required.predictors = a list of fixed effects that you require in the model
  # predictors = a list of your fixed effects that may be removed
  # random = your random effect as a string, example "(1|site/plot_id)"
  # stat.dist = the "family" of the model exactly as you would want it input, e.g. Gamma(link = "log") 
  
  formula <- as.formula(paste(response, "~",
                              paste(c(required.predictors), collapse = " + "), "+",
                              paste(c(predictors), collapse = " + "), "+", random))
  
  gm <- glmmTMB(formula, family = stat.dist, data = df)
  
  converged <-  FALSE
  output <- as.data.frame(matrix(nrow = 0, ncol = 6))
  p <- 1

  while (converged == FALSE) {

    print(length(predictors))

    coef.table <- rownames_to_column(data.frame(coef(summary(gm))$cond),
                                     var = "factor")
    
    words_to_remove <- "open|caged|large|small|April|May|June|July|August"
    
    coef.table <- coef.table %>% 
      mutate(factor = str_remove_all(factor, words_to_remove))
    
    # Subset rows where the Estimate is NA
    coef.select <- coef.table[coef.table$factor %in% predictors,]
    row <- coef.select[which.max(coef.select$Pr...z..),]
    print(row)
    p <- row$Pr...z..
    remove <- row$factor
    print(paste("remove: ", remove))

    predictors <- setdiff(predictors, remove)
    print(predictors)

    if (length(predictors) == 1) {
      converged <- TRUE
      print(converged)
    }

    formula <- as.formula(paste(response, "~",
                          paste(c(required.predictors), collapse = " + "), "+",
                          paste(c(predictors), collapse = " + "), "+", random))
      
      print(formula)
  
    gm <- glmmTMB(formula, family = stat.dist, data = df)

    print(AIC(gm))

    output <- rbind(output, cbind(row, AIC(gm)))

  }
  return(output)
}
```

# QUESTION 1: What biotic and abiotic factors drive kelp survival?
```{r}
# Starting with all predictors

#predictors.survival <- c("urchin_site_density", "ts_site_density", "urchin_density", "ts_density", "max_temperature_c", "mean_temperature_c", "mean_light_lux", "mean_current", "bottom_salinity", "bottom_do", "treatment:month", "treatment:gravel_size", "gravel_size:month") # Uncomment for all regressors

# Removed mean temperature because it covaries with max temperature in the final model and was the least significant in the original global model

#predictors.survival <- c("urchin_site_density", "ts_site_density", "urchin_density", "ts_density", "max_temperature_c", "mean_light_lux", "mean_current", "bottom_do", "bottom_salinity", "treatment:month", "treatment:gravel_size", "gravel_size:month")

# Removed bottom salinity because it covaries with bottom do in the final model and was the least significant in the updated global model

predictors.survival <- c("urchin_site_density", "ts_site_density", "urchin_density", "ts_density", "max_temperature_c", "mean_light_lux", "mean_current", "bottom_do", "treatment:month", "treatment:gravel_size", "gravel_size:month")

formula <- as.formula(paste("cbind(n_kelp_gravel, n_gravel - n_kelp_gravel) ~ treatment + gravel_size + month +",
            paste(c(predictors.survival), collapse = " + "), 
            "+ (1 | site)"))

global.model <- glmmTMB(formula, family = binomial, data = data)

summary(global.model)
Anova(global.model)
```

# Selecting best model
```{r}
output <- select.model(data, "cbind(n_kelp_gravel, n_gravel - n_kelp_gravel)", c("treatment", "gravel_size", "month"), predictors.survival, "(1 | site)", binomial)

plot(output$`AIC(gm)`)
```

# Setting and examining the optimal model
```{r}
optimal.model <- glmmTMB(cbind(n_kelp_gravel, n_gravel - n_kelp_gravel) ~ treatment + 
    gravel_size + month + urchin_site_density + ts_site_density + 
    max_temperature_c + mean_light_lux + mean_current + bottom_do + 
    treatment:month + treatment:gravel_size + (1 | site), family = binomial, data = data)

summary(optimal.model)
Anova(optimal.model)

#Type 3 - Anova (with interactions)
Anova(optimal.model, type = 3)
```

# Plotting figure for the interaction between treatment and month
```{r}
# Plotting main treatment effect
summary <- data %>%                          
  group_by(treatment) %>%
  summarise_at(vars(kelp_survival),
               list(mean = ~mean(as.numeric(.), na.rm = TRUE),
                    sd = ~sd(as.numeric(.), na.rm = TRUE),
                    n = ~sum(!is.na(.))))
summary$se <- summary$sd/sqrt(summary$n)

ggplot(summary, aes(x = treatment, y = mean)) +
  geom_bar(position="dodge", stat="identity") +       
         xlab("Treatment") +
         ylab("Survival") +
         theme_bw()

# Plotting interaction between treatment and month
summary <- data %>%                          
  group_by(treatment, month) %>%
  summarise_at(vars(kelp_survival),
               list(mean = ~mean(as.numeric(.), na.rm = TRUE),
                    sd = ~sd(as.numeric(.), na.rm = TRUE),
                    n = ~sum(!is.na(.))))
summary$se <- summary$sd/sqrt(summary$n)

ggplot(summary, aes(x = month, y = mean, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_bar(position="dodge", stat="identity") +       
         xlab("Month") +
         ylab("Survival") +
         theme_bw()
```

# Checking model fit and normality
```{r include=FALSE}
# Check for overdispersion
testDispersion(optimal.model)

simulationOutput <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = optimal.model, plot = T)
simulationOutput

# Save the testDispersion plot
png(paste(path, "plots", "models", "survival_testDispersion_plot.png", sep = "/"), width = 800, height = 600)
testDispersion(optimal.model)
dev.off()

# Save the QQ plot
png(paste(path, "plots", "models", "survival_QQ_plot.png", sep = "/"), width = 800, height = 600)
plotQQunif(simulationOutput)  # Generate QQ plot
dev.off()

# Save residual vs predictor plot
png(paste(path, "plots", "models", "survival_residuals_vs_predictor.png", sep = "/"), width = 800, height = 600)
plotResiduals(simulationOutput)
dev.off()
```

# CONCLUSIONS: Kelp survival was significantly lower in open plots and on small gravel. Kelp survived significantly less in June, and there was an interaction between caging and month where caging was beneficial in May but not in April. Kelp survival significantly decreased with increasing urchin site density and mean light lux. Kelp survival significantly increased with increasing maximum temperature and bottom dissolved oxygen. This may be because these conditions also correlated with increased urchin densities in the urchin model.

# QUESTION 2: What biotic and abiotic factors drive kelp length?

# Recommend using each length measurement as a distinct data point, with plot nested in site as a random effect. This requires some re-organizing of data sheets.

```{r}
# Load original kelp length data
data.length.raw <- read.csv(paste(path, "data", "cleaned_green_gravel_monitoring.csv", sep = "/"))

data.length.raw$month <- factor(data.length.raw$month, levels = c("April", "May", "June"))
data.length.raw$plot_unique <- paste(data.length.raw$month, data.length.raw$site, data.length.raw$plot_id)
```

# Creating kelp length data sheet
```{r}
# Make each kelp length measurement its own row
data.length <- data.length.raw %>%
      pivot_longer(kelp_total1:kelp_total5, names_to = "kelp_individual", values_to = "kelp_length_cm")

# Remove zero data, which were supposed to be NA in original data table
data.length <- data.length[!data.length$kelp_length_cm == 0,]

# Merge with environmental variables for each plot and timepoint
data.length <- merge(data.length[c("plot_unique", "kelp_length_cm")], data, by = "plot_unique")
```

# Creating global model
```{r}
# All
predictors.length <- c("urchin_site_density", "ts_site_density", "urchin_density", "ts_density", "mean_temperature_c", "max_temperature_c", "mean_light_lux", "mean_current", "bottom_salinity", "bottom_do", "treatment:month", "treatment:gravel_size", "gravel_size:month")

formula <- as.formula(paste("kelp_length_cm ~ treatment + gravel_size + month + ",
            paste(c(predictors.length), collapse = " + "), 
            "+ (1 | site/plot_id)"))

global.model <- glmmTMB(formula, family = Gamma(link = "log"), data = data.length)

summary(global.model)
```

# Selecting best model
```{r}
output <- select.model(data.length, "kelp_length_cm", c("treatment", "gravel_size", "month"), predictors.length, "(1 | site/plot_id)", Gamma(link = "log"))

plot(output$`AIC(gm)`)
```

# Setting and examining the optimal model
```{r}
optimal.model <- glmmTMB(kelp_length_cm ~ treatment + gravel_size + month + urchin_site_density + ts_site_density + mean_temperature_c + mean_light_lux + mean_current + bottom_salinity + urchin_density + gravel_size:month + (1 | site/plot_id), family = Gamma(link = "log"), data = data.length)

summary(optimal.model)
Anova(optimal.model)

#Type 3 - Anova (with interactions)
Anova(optimal.model, type = 3)

# Lowest AIC included urchin plot density. I removed this in final model because doing so only negligibly raised the AIC while decreasing the complexity of model, and including it made the residuals worse. Urchin plot density was not significant. Excluding it did not change the significance of any other factor except it made treatment significant, which is expected because treatment significantly influences grazer density inside plots.
```

# Visualizing model relationships
```{r}
visreg(optimal.model)
visreg(optimal.model, "gravel_size", by = "month")
```

```{r include=FALSE}
simulationOutput

```

# CONCLUSIONS: Caging significantly increased kelp length. Gravel size interacted with month such that kelp were smaller on small gravel in May but larger on small gravel in June. Kelp length significantly decreased with increasing urchin site density, turban snail site density, mean temperature, mean current, and bottom salinity. Kelp length significantly increased with increasing mean light lux.
